sentences: Treat isolated myofibers with associated satellite cells with tibialis anterior muscle extracts in floating culture for 24 hours.
Perform immunofluorescence studies on satellite cells treated with muscle extracts and control myofibers in DMEM using markers PAX7, MYOD, Ki67, and EdU.
Mechanically damage healthy intact myofibers from extensor digitorum longus muscles using a Pasteur pipette.
Co-culture intact myofibers with damaged myofibers for 48 hours and 72 hours.
Perform immunofluorescence analysis on co-cultured myofibers using markers MYOD, Ki67, and EdU.
Wash out damaged myofibers and culture media from co-cultured myofibers and culture for 24 hours.
Replace the culture media of myofibers with washed culture media with fresh DMEM.
Perform proteome analysis on supernatant from intact and damaged myofiber conditions using SDS-PAGE in the range of 10 to 50 kDa.
Treat isolated myofibers with associated satellite cells with recombinant proteins AK-1, CK, GAPDH, PGAM-2, and TPI in floating culture for 72 hours.
Perform immunostaining on satellite cells treated with recombinant proteins using markers MYOD and PAX7.
Treat isolated myofibers with associated satellite cells with metabolic enzymes AK-1, CK, and GAPDH in non-glucose medium.
Test the effect of c-MET inhibitor PHA-665752 on satellite cell activation in satellite cells treated with recombinant DMDFs.
Test the effect of signaling pathway inhibitors Rapamycin, SU5402, Wortmannin, PD98059, and Dorsomorphin on satellite cell entry into G1 phase in satellite cells treated with recombinant GAPDH.
Pre-treat satellite cells associated with myofibers with recombinant enzyme proteins AK-1, CK, GAPDH, TPI, and PGAM-2 in floating culture for 48 hours.
Stimulate satellite cells pre-treated with recombinant enzymes with growth-factor-rich medium (GM) for 24 hours.
Administer recombinant GAPDH protein into TA muscles 24 hours prior to BaCl2 injection.
Induce muscle regeneration in TA muscles treated with recombinant GAPDH by BaCl2 injection.
Perform qPCR analysis on muscle tissue from GAPDH-pre-treated mice for genes Pax7 and MyoD.
Perform immunohistochemistry on regenerating muscles from GAPDH-pre-treated mice using markers PAX7 and EdU.

sentences: Obtain ethics approval for the use of human specimens from the Ethics Reviewing Board of the University Hospital of Liege, Belgium with reference number 2020/119.

Select human biopsy specimens including lung postmortem biopsy specimens and biopsy specimens from liver, heart, kidney, and pancreas from four SARS-CoV-2 patients and four non-COVID-19 patients matched for age and sex provided by the Biobank of the Liege University Hospital.
Perform H&E staining on human biopsy specimens prior to selection by two pathologists.

Analyze hematology and biochemistry using blood samples from COVID-19 patients with retrospective analysis of the last available blood sample taken within 24 hours preceding the patient's death conducted by the central laboratory of the Liege University Hospital.
Prepare FFPE tissue sections by cutting formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded lung biopsy specimens into 4 µm sections for histological and immunofluorescence examination.
Digitize H&E-stained lung tissue slides using a Pannoramic 250 Flash III Scanner.

Score histopathological lesions on digitized H&E-stained slides by having two experienced pathologists assess high-resolution images focusing on NET areas using a scoring system for lesions typically found in SARS-CoV-2 diffuse alveolar damage.

Perform immunofluorescence staining on lung tissue sections by deparaffinizing, rehydrating, boiling in sodium carbonate buffer for antigen retrieval, permeabilizing with PBS 0.5% Triton X-100, blocking with blocking buffer, staining with rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 antibodies and goat anti-human MPO antibodies followed by secondary donkey anti-rabbit IgG and donkey anti-goat IgG antibodies, counterstaining with DAPI, mounting with ProLong Antifade reagent, and storing overnight.
Acquire images with fluorescence microscopy using standard filter sets on stained lung tissue samples.
Perform control staining by incubating with secondary antibodies after treatment with sera from host species without primary antibodies to check for nonspecific fluorescent staining.
Acquire and process images using a Zeiss LSM 880 Airyscan Elyra S.1. confocal microscope and ImageJ software.

Quantify NET volume by analyzing six fields per patient from lung tissue images, acquiring Z-stack pictures, performing three-dimensional reconstruction, and quantifying the volume of structures double positive for Cit-H3 and MPO using Imaris software.

Run Imaris scripts for colocalization analysis on .ims files using Imaris script/macro tools by thresholding staining, creating an intersection channel, measuring the volume of the intersection and total volume of the picture, and generating an Excel .xlsx file with measurements.
Scan entire lung sections at 0.46 µm/pixel resolution using the Nanozoomer 2.0-HT system and TRI-CCD camera and manually screen for NET-infiltrating areas.
Perform statistical analysis on data from immunofluorescence analysis using the nonparametric Mann–Whitney U test on mean values to determine statistical significance.

sentences: Enrich 2x10^6 A-CD8+ T cells.
Stimulate 2x10^6 A-CD8+ T cells with 1x10^6 B-APCs mismatched at HLA-A, -B, and -DR with individual A.
Add cytokines IL-2 at 20 U/ml, IL-7 at 50 ng/ml, and IL-15 at 50 ng/ml to the culture.
Incubate cells in 24-well plates for 9 days.
Enrich in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells.
Label 5x10^4 A-CD4+ T cells per well with CFSE.
Coculture 5x10^4 A-CD4+ T cells per well with B-APCs or I-APCs mismatched at HLA-A, -B, and -DR with individual A and B for I-APCs.
Add 2.5x10^4 in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells per well to the coculture.
Incubate the coculture in a 96-well round bottom plate for 7 days and 11 days.
Assess proliferation of CD4+ T cells using the CFSE dilution assay.

sentences: Screen publicly available datasets to identify Arabidopsis genes with transcriptional signatures of CBGs or CCGs, resulting in the identification of At2g35260 as BCM1.
Perform immunoblot analyses using BCM1 antiserum to determine BCM1 accumulation in Arabidopsis tissues, finding that BCM1 accumulates as a ~36 kDa protein except in roots.
Analyze BCM1 transcript to compare its expression pattern with key CBGs, revealing that BCM1 clusters with key CBGs and shows similar expression to GUN4.
Characterize BCM1 protein and determine that it is a 382-amino-acid protein with a chloroplast transit peptide and six transmembrane domains.
Perform transient expression assay with BCM1-YFP fusion to determine chloroplast localization of BCM1, confirming its localization to chloroplast.
Conduct immunoblot analyses on isolated chloroplast fractions to determine BCM1 distribution, showing that 92% of BCM1 is in the thylakoid membrane and 8% in the envelope.
Treat isolated thylakoids with chaotropic and alkaline reagents to test if BCM1 is an integral or peripheral thylakoid protein, demonstrating that BCM1 behaves like integral LHC proteins.

Characterize bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX plants to investigate BCM1 function in chlorophyll biosynthesis, revealing that BCM1 is important for chlorophyll accumulation and affects ALA synthesis and Mg-porphyrin flux.

Examine expression of CBGs and levels of CBEs using immunoblot and qRT-PCR analyses to understand BCM1's role in chlorophyll biosynthesis, showing that BCM1 acts post-translationally and is not implicated in proteolysis of CBEs.

Investigate genetic interaction between BCM1 and MgCh to clarify their roles in MgCh activity, finding that BCM1 deficiency exacerbates growth phenotypes and affects leaf pigmentation and MgCh activity.
Perform yeast two-hybrid screen to identify potential BCM1 partners in the TBS pathway, discovering that BCM1 interacts with GluTR, GUN4, and CHLM.

Explore the effect of BCM1 on MgCh activity using in vitro assays with recombinant MgCh components to determine the necessity of BCM1-GUN4 interaction for MgCh activity stimulation, confirming that BCM1 interacts with GUN4 and stimulates MgCh activity.
Analyze BCM1 orthologs to study their conservation in land plants, finding that BCM1 orthologs are conserved but not found in green algae or cyanobacteria.
Identify BCM1 paralog and determine that BCM2 is a paralog of BCM1 in Arabidopsis.

Quantify contributions of BCM paralogs to chlorophyll biosynthesis using T-DNA insertion knockdown mutants and double mutant analyses to optimize chlorophyll biosynthesis, showing that BCM1 predominantly regulates chlorophyll biosynthesis while BCM2 acts in late stages.

Generate bcm1-2 complementation lines with 35S promoter-driven BCM2 expression to test if BCM2 can compensate for BCM1 deficiency, demonstrating that BCM2 functionally substitutes for BCM1 in chlorophyll biosynthesis.

Determine chlorophyll degradation rates using dark-induced senescence of detached leaves to investigate the function of BCM paralogs in chlorophyll catabolism, revealing that BCM1/2 overexpression delays chlorophyll breakdown while bcm1-3 bcm2-2 enhances it.

Conduct electron microscopic analyses to observe chloroplast structure during chlorophyll breakdown, showing that BCM1/2 overexpression retains intact thylakoid membranes while bcm1-3 bcm2-2 shows degradation.

Dissect the molecular mechanism of BCM isoforms in chlorophyll catabolism to understand how BCMs prevent chlorophyll breakdown, finding that BCM1/2 overproduction destabilizes SGR1 and inhibits chlorophyll breakdown.

sentences: Verify compliance with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Georgia State University under protocol A11025 approved from 2011-08-30 to 2014-08-30.
Acquire 8-week-old C57BL/6 mice weighing between 18 and 22 grams from Jackson Laboratories in Bar Harbor, ME.
House animals at 25 degrees Celsius with a 12:12-hour light–dark cycle and provide access to standard mouse chow and tap water.
Administer 3% (wt/vol) DSS with a molecular weight of 40000 Da in drinking water for 7 days using DSS supplied by ICN Biochemicals in Aurora, OH.
Euthanize animals using CO2 euthanasia 7 days post-treatment.
Collect 50 mg tissue samples from the proximal colon.
Extract RNA using TRIzol reagent from Life Technologies in Carlsbad, CA following the manufacturer's instructions.
Assess RNA integrity by 2% agarose gel electrophoresis.

Purify RNA by lithium chloride precipitation following these steps: incubate with 8 M LiCl at a volume ratio of 0.1 at 0 degrees Celsius for 2 hours; centrifuge at 14000 g and 4 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes; discard supernatant; resuspend pellet in 200 µL RNase-free water; repeat incubation and centrifugation; precipitate RNA with 0.1 volume 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2 and 2 volumes 100% absolute ethanol at -20 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes; centrifuge at 14000 g and 4 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes; discard supernatant; wash pellet with 100 µL 70% ethanol; centrifuge at 14000 g and 4 degrees Celsius for 10 minutes; discard supernatant; and resuspend RNA in 20 to 50 µL RNase-free water.
Synthesize cDNA using the Maxima First-Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit from Thermo Scientific in Waltham, MA following the manufacturer's instructions.

Perform qPCR using Maxima SYBR Green/ROX qPCR Master Mix from Thermo Scientific with primers 36B4-F (TCCAGGCTTTGGGCATCA) and 36B4-R (CTTTATCAGCTGCACATCACTCAGA) on a Realplex Thermal Cycler from Eppendorf in Hauppauge, NY.

Measure polymerase activity using the EvaEZ™ Fluorometric Polymerase Activity Assay kit from Eppendorf in Hayward, CA following the manufacturer's instructions with recombinant Taq DNA polymerase (0.01 units) from Thermo Scientific, DSS at concentrations of 0.01 and 1 g/L, and Dextran as control on a Realplex Thermal Cycler with fluorescence readout every 1 minute for 60 minutes at 72 degrees Celsius.

Measure reverse transcriptase activity using the EnzChek Reverse Transcriptase Assay kit from Biotek in Carlsbad, CA following the manufacturer's instructions with 0.4 units M-MuLV RT, DSS at concentrations of 5e-05 and 0.0005 g/L, standardized polyA RNA template, oligodT primers, polymerization buffer at 25 degrees Celsius on a Synergy 2 Multi-Mode Microplate Reader with fluorescence readout.

Perform SPR experiments using the BI-2000 SPR from Biosensing Instrument in Tempe, AZ, USA by cleaning and treating the gold chip as described in references 22, 23, and 24; activate the biosensor chip with EDC/NHS to form amide linkages; inject 2400 units of reverse transcriptase twice after purification using Slide-A-Lyser® Mini dialysis devices in PBS; flow primed RNA over the chip twice at 42 degrees Celsius with random primers and DSS at concentrations of 0.05, 0.5, and 5 g/L; and measure laser deviation angle in mDegrees (mDeg).
Perform statistical analysis representing data as means ± SEM using an unpaired two-tailed t-test in GraphPad Prism 5 with significance threshold p < 0.05.

sentences: Collect 166 blood samples from 41 patients (68% female) aged 11–80 years admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong, from March to May 2003.
Test 7 blood samples for SARS-CoV using RT-PCR.
Culture cell lines in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium with Glutamax and high glucose supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum and penicillin/streptomycin.
Clone the human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) gene from a human primary kidney cDNA library into the pcdna3.1+ vector.
Transfect QT6 cells using lipofectamine 2000 and select with G418.
Split 293T cells at a ratio of 1:4 one day before transfection.
Transfect 293T cells with 1 μg gag/pol construct, 1.5 μg enhanced GFP reporter construct, and 1.5 μg envelope-expressing construct using Fugene-6.
Harvest supernatant at 48 h and 72 h posttransfection, filter through 0.45-μm filters, and store at -80°C.
Measure MLV and HIV vector titer as infectious units per milliliter in 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells by detecting eGFP titers at 72 h post-infection using a fluorescence-activated cell sorter.
Heat inactivate patient serum samples at 56°C for 30 min.
Dilute heat-inactivated patient serum samples serially starting at 1:10 in culture medium.
Mix serum dilution with 50 PFU SARS Frankfurt strain and incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 5 × 10^4 Vero E6 cells per well to the virus and serum mix in 96-well plates and incubate for 4 days to assess cytopathic effect and determine the last well with complete neutralization.
Assay serum samples in duplicate and confirm with separate assays.
Dilute heat-inactivated patient serum samples 2-fold serially starting at 1:10 in culture medium.
Mix serum dilution with approximately 100 IU MLV(SARS) virions at a 1:1 vol/vol ratio and incubate at 37°C for 1 h.

Add 100 μL of serum and virion mix to QT6/ACE2 cells seeded at 1 × 10^4 cells per well in 96-well flat-bottomed tissue culture plates 24 h prior and detect GFP-positive cells at 48 h post-infection using fluorescence microscopy, presenting geometric mean titers from triplicate replicates.

sentences: Scan the cloned HAG maize CoREGs for the presence of an acetyl-CoA-binding site using the Conserved Domain Database (CDD).
Use the region of approximately 75–90 amino acids as the operational taxonomic unit for phylogenetic analysis.
Align related proteins using Clustal W with default parameters implemented using the megalign program within the dnastar Lasergene package.
Align AUX/IAA CoREGs FL amino acid sequences using MUSCLE with default parameters.
Export each multiple sequence alignment in Newick format.
Display phylogenetic trees using FigTree V1.4.0.
Clone constructs into either the pENTR/D-TOPO or pENTR/SD/D-TOPO vector.
Amplify targeted TF or CoREG ORFs using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with the manufacturer's GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol.
Optimize amplification by adding up to 10% DMSO, up to 4 mM MgCl2 or adjusting the annealing temperature if necessary.
Design primers to produce a fragment without a stop codon and with a 5'-CACC nucleotide tailing added to the forward primer for directional cloning into the pENTR vectors.
Screen kanamycin-resistant colonies for inserts of the correct size and orientation by colony PCR or by restriction digestion of candidate plasmids.
Confirm the sequence of cloned inserts by single-read paired-end Sanger dideoxy sequencing.
Design internal primers to complete the sequence confirmation for clones longer than 1200 bp.
Grow the B73 inbred of maize in a field nursery and isolate DNA for PCR amplification of single-exon genes or RNA for RT-PCR.
Determine codon optimization strategy for synthesized ORFs by analyzing pENTRSD/D-TOPO clones harboring synthesized coding sequences optimized according to maize, yeast or hybrid preference.
Use LR Clonase to recombine these CDSs into a GAL4-BD-GWC1 vector to fuse them with the yeast GAL4-binding domain or to generate N-terminal fusions with GFP into plasmid p1511.
Transform PJ69.4a yeast cells with each GAL4-BD-GWC1 construct using the lithium acetate/single-stranded carrier DNA/polyethylene glycol method.
Prepare protein samples from yeast cells for Western blot analysis.
Perform Western blot analysis using the prepared protein samples.
Digest maize leaves to prepare protoplasts for transformation.
Electroporate protoplasts with DNA for transient luciferase assays and transient complementation assays.
Estimate transformation efficiency following GFP expression under a fluorescence microscope.
Quantify fluorescence using intensity measurement of the entire protoplast area using Image J software.
Isolate genomic DNA from B73 plant tissue using a CTAB-based method.
Isolate total RNA from non-starchy B73 tissues using RNAzol according to the manufacturer's suggested protocol.
Isolate RNA from starchy tissues such as developing seeds using a modified protocol.
Verify RNA integrity by agarose gel electrophoresis and ethidium bromide staining.
Treat total RNA samples with Turbo DNA-free to remove any contaminating DNA.
Synthesize complementary DNA using Maxima H Minus Reverse Transcriptase.
Verify the integrity of cDNA by amplifying a portion of a Zm GAPDH transcript.
Perform RT-PCR on tissues where TFs are expected to be most highly expressed.

sentences: Sow Phaseolus vulgaris seeds of genotypes Black Valentine, JaloEEP558, BAT93, G19833, TU, DOR364, and La Victoire in vermiculite.
Grow seedlings in a growth chamber at 23°C with a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity for 10-12 days.
Transplant 3 seedlings into moist vermiculite in a 20 cm plastic pot in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation.
Grow 77 F11 RILs derived from a cross between JaloEEP558 and BAT93 in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation and phenotype them 7 days post-inoculation.
Construct RNA2-derived plasmids using P. vulgaris target gene fragments, Bam H1 restriction site, and pBPMV-IA-V1 in the laboratory.
Clone the double-stranded synthetic oligonucleotide containing the Bam H1 restriction site to produce BPMV-PvPDS-52 bp.
Amplify target gene fragments by PCR using specific primers, P. vulgaris cDNAs, and high fidelity polymerase with a PCR machine.
Digest PCR products with Bam H1 using restriction enzymes.
Ligate the digested fragments into Bam H1-digested and dephosphorylated pBPMV-IA-V1 vector using ligase.
Determine the orientation of cloned inserts by PCR using vector-specific and fragment-specific primers.
Sequence clones with antisense orientation using the sequencing service at GATC, Germany.
Prepare a 20 μL DNA-plasmid mix in 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer at pH 7.0.
Perform rub-inoculation by mechanical rubbing of the DNA-plasmid mix and infected leaf sap on one primary leaf unless otherwise stated.
Grow inoculated plants in a growth chamber at 19°C with a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle.
Evaluate GFP expression using a UV lamp for aerial organs and roots, a digital camera, and a microscope for roots at 21 dpi.
Perform semi-quantitative RT-PCR with total RNA, cDNA, and specific primers using a PCR machine for 25 cycles and analyze by agarose-ethidium bromide electrophoresis.
Map the R-BPMV resistance gene using MAPMAKER software version 3.0 with Chi-squared test, LOD threshold, and Kosambi mapping function.

sentences: Obtain approval for mouse work from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee in compliance with Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare guidelines.

Use mouse strains including C57BL/6, Tlr7 −/−, Tlr9 −/−, Myd88 −/−, and Tlr7 -/- Tlr9 -/- double knockout obtained from Jackson Laboratories, National Cancer Institute, R Medzhitov at Yale University, and J Cox at UCSF with permissions from S Akira at Osaka University and T Taniguchi at University of Tokyo, ensuring a C57BL/6 background greater than 95% and verification by microsatellite genotyping.
Maintain P. berghei strain ANKA parasites from the MR4 stock centre in C57BL/6 mice.
Harvest blood by cardiac puncture on day 5 of infection for infection initiation.
Introduce 10^6 infected erythrocytes by intraperitoneal injection in 100 μl Alsever’s solution at 14.00 hours.
Harvest blood by submandibular blood collection or cardiac puncture into K2 EDTA tubes for plasma isolation for cytokine analysis.
Monitor survival and signs of cerebral malaria daily and twice daily from days 6 through 12.
Consider cerebral malaria if convulsions, ataxia, or paralysis occur on or before day 12 post-infection.
Monitor parasitaemia daily using Giemsa-stained thin film blood smears.
Assess significance of parasitaemia courses using the Mann–Whitney U test with an alpha of 0.05.
Assess significance of survival courses by comparing Kaplan-Meier curves using the log rank (Mantel-Cox) test with an alpha of 0.05.
Measure plasma cytokines using multiplexed cytometric bead immunoassay on a MAGPIX (Luminex) instrument from Millipore.
Assess cytokine level significance using the Mann–Whitney U test with an alpha of 0.05.
